alerts.title: DTG-associated hyperglycemia: pre-diabetes in high-risk patient
alerts.message: Guidelines state hyperglycemia has been reported in non-diabetic adults on DTG, and clients with ≥2 hyperglycemia risk factors require glucose monitoring. This patient has multiple risk factors: age ≥30, family history of DM, BMI ≥25. Since switching to DTG 18 months ago, fasting glucose rose from 92 to 118 mg/dL (impaired) and HbA1c is 6.1% (pre-diabetic). Acanthosis nigricans confirms insulin resistance. Evidence for DTG attribution: temporal relationship with DTG initiation, 17kg weight gain, and guideline-recognized association. Evidence against: family history of DM and chronic inflammation from HIV also contribute. No clinician plan was documented for this finding.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess for diabetes per DM screening algorithm. Consider DTG substitution if hyperglycemia worsens. Monitor fasting glucose or HbA1c every 3 months. Provide lifestyle counseling for weight and diet.

alerts.title: Significant weight gain and dyslipidemia on DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines identify rapid weight gain and dyslipidemia as ART-related metabolic complications. Since DTG initiation 18 months ago, patient gained 17kg (65kg to 82kg), BMI shifted from 25.6 to 32.4 kg/m² (obese), waist circumference 96cm, and BP rose from 118/74 to 138/88 mmHg. Lipid profile is markedly abnormal: LDL 148, HDL 38, triglycerides 212, total cholesterol 228 mg/dL. DTG is associated with greater weight gain than EFV. Evidence for drug attribution: weight gain temporally followed DTG switch and guidelines recognize this association. Evidence against: dietary and lifestyle factors not assessed. No clinician plan addresses these metabolic changes.

evidence.recommended_action: Evaluate cardiovascular risk. Consider dietary and exercise counseling, lipid-lowering therapy per guidelines, and possible regimen review given magnitude of metabolic deterioration.

alerts.title: No documented assessment or plan for abnormal findings
alerts.message: Patient presents with pre-diabetic fasting glucose, abnormal HbA1c, significant dyslipidemia, new-onset hypertension-range BP, 17kg weight gain, and acanthosis nigricans. Guidelines require assessment for diabetes risk factors among patients on ART and appropriate follow-up. No clinician assessment or plan was documented for any of these findings. This represents a guideline deviation as the DM screening algorithm requires action when risk factors and abnormal glucose are present.

evidence.recommended_action: Document assessment and management plan addressing hyperglycemia, dyslipidemia, weight gain, and elevated BP. Complete diabetes screening per algorithm and initiate appropriate interventions.
